column1: # Case table for substrate/.github/workflows/auto-release-min.yml
# TAB-separated: <name> <context k=v;k=v> <expect-run csv> <expect-skip csv>
# WHAT THIS FILE PINS. auto-release-min is the bisect probe of the release
# family: detect the repo type, hand a caixa repo to the real release workflow,
# and fail loudly on anything else. Its whole contract is a two-arm PARTITION of
# detect's output — exactly one of `caixa`/`unsupported` runs, always. The rows
# below assert both arms so the partition cannot silently become "neither"
# (flip `!=` to `==` and every non-caixa repo goes green having released
# nothing) or "both" (an inverted arm double-dispatches).
# WHY THERE IS NO PRIVACY-SKIP ROW HERE, unlike cargo-auto-release.cases.tsv.
# `github.event.repository.private` appears twice in this workflow and BOTH
# occurrences are in `runs-on` — they pick a billing label, not a job. No `if:`
# in this file reads privacy, so no job here can be privacy-skipped and there is
# nothing honest to assert as one. Asserting a skip that the workflow cannot
# produce would be a row that reads as coverage and is not.
# The key is still declared in every case, on purpose: it is a TRIPWIRE. The day
# someone adds `&& !github.event.repository.private` to the `caixa` arm — the
# exact edit that made graphql-synthesizer ship nothing while reporting success —
# the private row below turns red with NOT-RUN, forcing the posture to be stated
# rather than acquired. Today it costs nothing and asserts nothing; it is here so
# that tomorrow it does.
# WHAT THIS FILE CANNOT SEE, stated so nobody reads its green as broader than it
# is. `caixa` is a `uses:` dispatch into caixa-tlisp-auto-release.yml. This
# linter models dispatch only — never the called workflow's own conditions. That
# delegate has one job (`release`, gated on actor, no privacy gate), and its
# publish is gated at STEP level (`steps.bump.outputs.bumped == 'true'`), which
# is below this tool's resolution entirely. "caixa ran" here means "the delegate
# was invoked", never "a release was published". The delegate needs its own
# table; this one does not cover it.
# The two arms are total, so a caixa repo's public/private rows select
# identically today. That is the finding, not an omission.
# A caixa repo is handed to the real release workflow; the catch-all stays quiet.
caixa-public
# TRIPWIRE ROW. Same selection as public, because dispatch here is unconditional
# on privacy. If this row ever disagrees with the one above, a privacy gate was
# added to the `caixa` arm and the posture must be written down here.
caixa-private
# The other arm of the partition: any repo type that is not caixa reaches the
# catch-all, which exits 1 on purpose. An unsupported repo must FAIL, never pass
# quietly — a probe that skips both arms is the silent-green shape this family
# exists to eliminate.
non-caixa-rust
# detect produced no output at all (its step set nothing). The empty string is a
# distinct state from any repo type, and it must still land in the catch-all
# rather than falling between the arms.
detect-yielded-nothing
